claims.text: Standard room-temperature laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys typically produces steep thermal gradients.
Standard room-temperature laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys typically produces heterogeneous microstructures.
Standard room-temperature laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys typically produces residual stresses.
Standard room-temperature laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys typically produces defects such as porosity and cracks.
Controlled build-chamber preheating reduces the temperature difference between the melt pool and surrounding material.
Reducing the melt-pool-to-surroundings temperature difference moderates the cooling rate.
Build-chamber preheating reduces thermal gradients during laser-based additive manufacturing of high-entropy alloys.
The moderated thermal environment produced by preheating reduces residual stresses.
Preheating produces a more uniform microstructure.
Preheating lessens the nucleation of pores and cracks.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stresses decrease defect formation.
Relative to room-temperature builds, preheated builds will have smaller deviations from the designed geometry.
Relative to room-temperature builds, preheated builds will have lower defect density.
Relative to room-temperature builds, preheated builds will have enhanced tensile properties.
Relative to room-temperature builds, preheated builds will have enhanced fatigue properties.
Under optimized processing conditions, the improvements caused by preheating should be statistically significant.
The benefits of preheating may diminish when the preheating temperature lies outside an alloy-specific optimal range.
The magnitude of the dimensional and mechanical improvement may vary with alloy composition and processing conditions.
